title_en: Case of the Republic of Korea's Request to the People's Republic of China for Extradition of Byun In-ho, a Citizen of the Republic of Korea
ruling_gist_en: According to the relevant provisions of the Extradition Law of the People's Republic of China and the Extradition Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Korea, a request by the Republic of Korea to extradite an offender from China must satisfy the dual criminality principle, i.e., the conduct alleged in the extradition request must constitute a crime under both the Criminal Code of the Republic of Korea and the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. Where the Republic of Korea requests extradition for the purpose of executing a sentence, the remaining term of imprisonment to be served by the person sought at the time of the request shall be no less than six months. If the Republic of Korea submits an extradition request based on a default judgment, it must undertake to grant the person sought an opportunity for a retrial in his or her presence after extradition; otherwise, the request will be refused by China. In this case, the Supreme People's Court has rendered a ruling that the extradition complies with the treaty, and it has also noted that Chinese judicial authorities are conducting criminal proceedings against Bian Renhao on suspicion of contract fraud committed within Chinese territory. The decision on whether to extradite Bian Renhao or to grant extradition but simultaneously defer it shall be made by the State Council of the People's Republic of China.

full_text_en:
Republic of Korea v. Byun In-ho — extradition case

【Ruling Summary】

According to the relevant provisions of the Extradition Law of the PRC and the Extradition Treaty between the PRC and the Republic of Korea, when the Republic of Korea requests extradition of a criminal from China, the principle of dual criminality must be satisfied, i.e., the conduct alleged in the extradition request must constitute a crime under both the Criminal Code of the Republic of Korea and the Criminal Law of the PRC. Where the Republic of Korea requests extradition for the purpose of executing a sentence, the unserved portion of the sentence at the time of the extradition request shall be not less than six months. If the Republic of Korea makes an extradition request based on a default judgment, it must undertake to provide the requested person with an opportunity for retrial in his presence after extradition; otherwise, the extradition will be refused by China. In this case, the Supreme People's Court has rendered a ruling that the extradition complies with the treaty, and has noted that the Chinese judicial authorities are conducting criminal proceedings against Byun In-ho for suspected contract fraud committed within China. The decision on whether to extradite Byun In-ho or to approve extradition while deferring it shall be made by the State Council of China.

Supreme People's Court Extradition Ruling

(2006) Xing Yin Zi No. 2

Requesting State for Extradition: the Republic of Korea.

Person Requested for Extradition: Byun In-ho, male, born on January 15, 1957, a citizen of the Republic of Korea, residing at 101-1308 Hyundai Apartment, 1502 Myeonmok 7-dong, Jungnang-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea; temporarily residing before arrest at Room 302, Xita Oriental Pearl, Heping District, Shenyang, Liaoning Province, PRC. He was placed under criminal detention on November 28, 2005 on suspicion of committing contract fraud within the PRC, placed under residential surveillance on December 27 of the same year, and arrested on April 30, 2006. He is currently detained at the Yingkou Detention Center, Liaoning Province.

On August 21, 1998, the Seoul Central District Court of the Republic of Korea sentenced Byun In-ho to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of KRW 2,000,000 for fraud. After the judgment, Byun In-ho appealed to the Seoul High Court. During the appellate proceedings, Byun In-ho took advantage of a suspension of detention for medical treatment and fled to the PRC. The Seoul High Court, in the absence of Byun In-ho, rendered a judgment on February 19, 1999 dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. On January 26, 2006, the Republic of Korea requested the PRC to extradite the criminal, Byun In-ho, a citizen of the Republic of Korea, to serve his sentence. This Court, in accordance with the Extradition Law of the PRC, and after the Republic of Korea undertook to provide the requested person with an opportunity for retrial in his presence after extradition, issued the "Designated Review Decision" (2006) Xing Yin Zi No. 2 on August 23, 2006, designating the Liaoning High People's Court to review the extradition request of the Republic of Korea. On December 18, 2006, the Liaoning High People's Court rendered Extradition Ruling (2006) Liao Xing Er Yin Zi No. 1, ruling that the request of the Republic of Korea for the extradition of Byun In-ho satisfied the conditions for granting extradition as stipulated in the Extradition Law of the PRC and the Extradition Treaty between the PRC and the Republic of Korea, and submitted the case to this Court for approval in accordance with the law. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review the case.

Upon review, this Court confirms that the conduct alleged in the Republic of Korea's extradition request, namely that Byun In-ho repeatedly defrauded the government of export tax rebates amounting to USD 300 million and KRW 400 billion, and illegally manipulated stock prices between February 1997 and August 1998, constitutes a crime under both the Criminal Law of the PRC and the Criminal Code of the Republic of Korea. Moreover, at the time the Republic of Korea made the extradition request, the unserved portion of the sentence of the requested person was not less than six months. The extradition request of the Republic of Korea for Byun In-ho satisfies the conditions for granting extradition as stipulated in the Extradition Law of the PRC and the Extradition Treaty between the PRC and the Republic of Korea. The extradition ruling of the Liaoning High People's Court is correct. During the review by this Court, the requested person Byun In-ho did not raise any new opinions. Pursuant to Article 26, item (1) of the Extradition Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

Approves the ruling of the Liaoning High People's Court, (2006) Liao Xing Er Yin Zi No. 1, which determined that the extradition request of the Republic of Korea for the requested person Byun In-ho satisfies the conditions for granting extradition as stipulated in the Extradition Law of the PRC and the Extradition Treaty between the PRC and the Republic of Korea.

This ruling shall become legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: Xue Shulan

Acting Judge: Yang Ke

Acting Judge: Chang Zhaohui

April 2, 2007

Clerk: Li Rui

【Presiding Judge Profile】

Xue Shulan, Senior Judge: born in 1954, Doctor of Laws, served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 1994.
